description: Four colonies with identical rules and one difference: rank. Every colony grows like Conway's Life and takes over rival cells, so wherever two colonies touch, the higher-ranked one wins the cell. Read the ladder by colour: green is lowest, then amber, then vermilion, and reddish-purple outranks everything. Four Ranks starts all four at once; Sandwich squeezes one colony between two stronger ones.

organisms.name: Conway's Classic
organisms.description: The original Game of Life rules: a cell is born with exactly 3 neighbors of its own kind and survives with 2 or 3, otherwise it dies. It can only defend, never take a cell from another organism, so in a mixed dish watch invaders eat into its colonies.

payload.summary: Born on an empty cell with exactly 3 neighbors

organisms.name: Lowly Moss
organisms.description: The bottom rung. It grows like Conway's Life and takes over any rival cell that has 2 or more Moss neighbors, but it loses every fight against a higher-ranked colony.

payload.summary: Takes over a rival cell with at least 2 neighbors of its own kind

organisms.name: Amber Squire
organisms.description: The second rung. It has the same habits as every rung of the ladder, and outranks Lowly Moss, but bows to Ember Knight and Violet Sovereign wherever they touch.

organisms.name: Ember Knight
organisms.description: The third rung. It beats Lowly Moss and Amber Squire at every contact line and yields only to Violet Sovereign.

organisms.name: Violet Sovereign
organisms.description: The top rung. Nobody outranks it, so at every contact line its colour is the one that advances. It still needs 2 neighbors of its own kind to take a rival cell.

battles.name: Sandwich
battles.description: Vermilion on the left, green in the middle, reddish-purple on the right. Both neighbors outrank the green colony, so it is squeezed from both sides; once it is gone, reddish-purple meets vermilion and outranks it too.

battles.name: Four Ranks
battles.description: Four colonies start in the four quarters of a 100x60 dish, one per rank. At every contact line the higher rank advances, so the lower colonies are pushed back and reddish-purple, which outranks all three, ends up holding most of the dish.
